scope: Exact-NCT observed clinical or FDA facts for active 258-trial research. These are not numerical clinical ratings, FDA probabilities or pre-readout predictions.
warnings: Published results are treated as post-readout observations only; publications cannot be used to backtest a prospective forecast unless before prediction cutoff.
Positive efficacy data and medical safety warnings never convert automatically to a clinical factor score.
Co-primary outcomes remain separate: e.g. RISE UP pain-crisis p=0.1213 did not establish significance.

facts.evidence: Peer-reviewed exact NCT ENERGIZE trial: Hb response met by 55/130 (42.3%) receiving mitapivat versus 1/64 (1.6%) receiving placebo; adjusted treatment difference approximately 41 percentage points. Observed comparative efficacy, not a score for clinical importance; independent minimal clinically important difference (MCID) not adjudicated.

Peer-reviewed ENERGIZE-T exact-NCT result: transfusion-reduction response in 52/171 (30%) mitapivat vs 11/87 (13%) placebo, adjusted treatment difference 18 percentage points (95% CI 8-27; p=0.0003). Observed outcome; no independent benefit-importance grade inferred.

ENERGIZE-T report: 238/258 patients (92%) completed the randomized double-blind period; study-treatment discontinuation for adverse events in 10 mitapivat patients (6%) and 1 placebo patient (1%). Cohort-level facts do not establish expected future retention.

RISE UP exact-NCT Lancet data must keep mixed co-primary evidence: hemoglobin response in 56/138 (41%) mitapivat vs 2/69 (3%) placebo, adjusted difference 38 percentage points, p<0.0001; sickle-cell pain-crisis rates 2.6 vs 3.1/year, p=0.1213 (not statistically significant). Do NOT mark both co-primary endpoints as successful.

RISE UP exact-NCT Lancet trial reported Hb improvements observed early and lasting median approximately 50 weeks during the randomized double-blind treatment period. This is within-trial follow-up, not evidence of sustained benefit after therapy is discontinued or an approved durability score.

FDA ROSELLA exact-NCT approval review: median PFS 6.5 vs 5.5 months with combination versus nab-paclitaxel alone (HR 0.70; 95% CI 0.54-0.91; p=0.0076); median OS 16.0 vs 11.9 months (HR 0.65; 95% CI 0.51-0.83; p=0.0004). Observed randomized effects, not numeric clinical-importance grades.

FDA relacorilant label/approval summary warns of neutropenia, severe infections, adrenal insufficiency and other risks. Warning presence is documented, not an independent adverse-event incidence comparison or acceptable-safety rating.

FDA approved relacorilant (Lifyorli) plus nab-paclitaxel on March 25, 2026 for the ROSELLA-specific platinum-resistant ovarian/fallopian/peritoneal cancer population, explicitly citing NCT05257408. Historical exact-trial regulatory result, not forecast for other indications or programs.

Phase 3 IMerge randomized exact-NCT Lancet report: at least 8-week red blood cell transfusion independence achieved by 47/118 (40%) imetelstat vs 9/60 (15%) placebo, treatment difference 25 percentage points (95% CI 9.9-36.9; p=0.0008). Severe cytopenias reported in treatment arm; no automatic clinical-importance score.

Phase 3 IMerge exact NCT published durable transfusion-independence analysis: duration among transfusion-independent responders approximately 51.6 weeks with imetelstat compared with 13.3 weeks with placebo. Selected responder-duration result, not unconditional duration in all randomized participants.

OASISplus exact-NCT open-label extension Year-1 cohort: mean Angioedema Quality of Life improvement at 52 weeks was 28.1 points (Q4W) and 26.7 (Q8W), compared with OASIS-HAE baseline; no concurrent randomized comparator. Paper describes threshold-based meaningful improvement; no trial-level calibrated clinical rating.

OASISplus exact-NCT 1-year open-label extension: 83 rolled-over patients, 75 completed Year 1, median donidalorsen exposure 392.3 days. Mean HAE attack-rate reductions from earlier OASIS-HAE baseline were 94% (Q4W) and 95% (Q8W) through 52 weeks; non-randomized extension cannot establish placebo-adjusted long-term effect.
OASISplus one-year open-label extension: 75/83 (90.4%) completed Year 1, 22/83 (27%) had treatment-related TEAEs, with no treatment-related serious AEs reported. Descriptive follow-up evidence only.

FDA September 3, 2026 approval of zilganersen (ZANVASTRO) explicitly identifies exact supporting pivotal study NCT04849741 in Alexander disease. Historical FDA result; not a retrospective clinical prediction, and no stand-alone binary primary endpoint score inferred.

TRANSCEND exact-NCT randomized data at 52 weeks: least-squares mean BMI change −16.5% setmelanotide versus +3.3% placebo (p<0.001); maximal hunger score changes −2.73 versus −1.45 (p=0.009). Serious adverse events occurred in 28% versus 8%. Observed endpoint values are not a safety or clinical-importance grade.

TRANSCEND exact-NCT published randomized 52-week BMI and hunger treatment results. Follow-up is 52 weeks on trial therapy; evidence of maintained benefit after discontinuation has not been established by this source, so no durability grade is inferred.

IMPALA-2 exact-NCT randomized report in autoimmune pulmonary alveolar proteinosis: mean DLCO change at Week 24 of 9.8 percentage points molgramostim vs 3.8 placebo, difference 6.0 points (95% CI 2.5-9.4; p<0.001). SGRQ-T difference reported; another SGRQ-A comparison not statistically significant, affecting secondary endpoint hierarchy. No independent clinical-importance grade.

IMPALA-2 exact-NCT randomized Week-48 observation: DLCO change 11.6 percentage points with molgramostim versus 4.7 placebo, both measured relative to baseline (p<0.001 for between-group contrast). On-treatment 48-week follow-up, not long-term post-treatment durability.

ORIGIN 3 final prespecified efficacy analysis in NCT04716231: at Week 52, mean eGFR change from baseline was -0.11 mL/min/1.73m2 for atacicept and -5.69 for placebo; between-arm difference 5.58 (95% CI 3.68 to 7.48; P<0.001). This is an observed randomized result, but a separate overall clinical-importance/RAAS grade is not inferred.

Exact-NCT ORIGIN 3 reported annualized eGFR slope through Week 104 of -0.60 with atacicept versus -5.60 mL/min/1.73m2 per year with placebo, difference 5.00 (95% CI 3.55 to 6.45; P<0.001). Controlled 104-week observation is documented; no assumption is made beyond follow-up or about future trials.

Exact-NCT ORIGIN 3 final report: adverse events were 160/214 (74.8%) on atacicept versus 167/214 (78.0%) on placebo; serious adverse events occurred in 7.0% versus 15.4%, respectively. Different safety event types and trial duration require interpretation; these counts are NOT a validated tolerability score.

ENVISION NCT05243550, a SINGLE-ARM Phase 3 UGN-102 study, reported complete response at Month 3 for 191/240 treated patients (80%; 95% CI 74-85%). No randomized comparator was included; the observed response must NOT be portrayed as placebo-adjusted efficacy, a clinical-importance grade or future approval probability.

ENVISION NCT05243550: among 191 patients with complete response at Month 3, estimated probability of remaining event-free 24 months after complete response was 72% (95% CI 64-79; Kaplan-Meier). This is a response-selected SINGLE-ARM group, not a randomized 24-month comparative treatment effect or evidence beyond follow-up.

ENVISION NCT05243550 trial enrolled 240 patients; 98% were White, 61% male, and 68% aged at least 65 years. The authors identified limited racial diversity as a study limitation. Demographics are observed site/population facts; generalizability to all intended users remains ungraded.

APeX-P NCT05453968 pediatric berotralstat open-label interim analysis (N=29): nasopharyngitis, upper respiratory infection and headache were common AEs; no reported drug-related grade 3/4 or serious AEs, deaths or AE-related discontinuations. The small uncontrolled cohort cannot establish comparative safety or a favorable risk score.

APeX-P NCT05453968: during the preceding standard-care period, median HAE attack rate was 0.96 per 4 weeks; median rates for successive 4-week intervals on open-label berotralstat were 0 through Week 48. This NONRANDOMIZED within-patient before/after comparison is a descriptive observation, NOT controlled efficacy or a clinical importance score.

APeX-P exact NCT open-label interim follow-up: at least 50% of analyzed children were attack-free in each individual 4-week interval through Week 48 on berotralstat (N=29 overall, variable exposure). Time-window evidence exists but a controlled long-term durability effect or calibrated RAAS score is NOT established.
